title: A spring ONI change term cut next-winter mean squared forecast error by 34% in two retrospective products for 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether the change from DJF to MAM adds information beyond MAM ONI for next-DJF forecasts. We fitted ordinary least squares to earlier issue years only. The 44 test winters were 1981-2024. Adding the change reduced mean squared error by 34.16% in ERSSTv5 and 34.21% in ERSSTv6. Conditional 95% five-year block limits were 15.25-47.14% and 15.41-46.74%. The gains were about 31% after three large warm-event winters were removed from scoring. Last-30-year training gave similar gains. A JJA change term gave about 8% added skill with limits that included zero. This is a test of a known linear forecast method, not a new physical explanation. The two products share observations. Retrospective reference periods, data revisions, few test winters and conditional intervals limit inference. The package gives 1,800 inputs, 1,056 predictions, coefficients, paired losses, source hashes, code, a figure and independent checks.

display.caption: Added forecast skill relative to a fitted level model and cumulative squared error saved. Bars give conditional 95% five-year block limits. Forecast targets are DJF 1981-2024.
